analysis.title: Credit Calls, Wednesday, October 28, 2026
key_insights: JPM upgrades Herc Rentals (HRI) to Overweight from Neutral. H&E integration risk is mostly retired, and with United Rentals now fully investment grade there are fewer high yield equipment rental bonds to own. Best value is the HRI 6s of '34.

O-I Glass (OI) 3Q26 adjusted EBITDA fell ~29% y/y to $234m versus Street $267m. Europe segment operating profit was $2m versus $95m a year earlier. FY26 guidance was cut again and JPM downgrades to Neutral. Gross and net leverage are 4.9x and 4.5x.

Boeing (BA) 3Q26 results were in line with free cash flow modestly ahead. First long-term FCF guidance for 2027-2029 came in below consensus, but better visibility is a credit positive. JPM stays Overweight with a 30-year fair value target of T+90bp, versus RTX at T+82bp, and expects the two to converge.
Custom Truck One Source (NSCO) 3Q26 earnings were in line, utility end-market demand is strong, and JPM reiterates Overweight. The 2L 5.5s of 2029 yield ~6.6%.
Johnson Controls (JCI) F4Q26 beat consensus on revenue, adjusted EBIT and FCF. Net leverage fell to ~1.8x. FY27 organic revenue growth guidance of 11-12% is well above 8.6% consensus.

Amkor Technology: in-line 3Q results that missed a high bar. Advanced packaging growth drivers remain intact, communications and consumer end-markets face headwinds, and focus stays on the capital expansion ramp into 2027.

CD Player trade idea: LQD call implied volatility has fallen in October while IEF implied volatility is sideways, so LQD calls are cheap relative to rates calls. Buying LQD calls funded by selling IEF calls gives a costless spread upside option.

Chemicals credit: FMC reports Thursday and its bonds remain $15-$20pt below levels before the 10/15 guidance revision. JPM stays Underweight FMC. JPM likes the CE-EMN CDS trade and sees room for LYB-DOW to compress.

HG credit curves: the 10s30s curve steepened 1.4bp WoW to 18bp, its steepest in a month. The hyperscaler 10s30s curve is 45bp, at 86% of its 1y range. The 2s30s UST curve flattened 11bp WoW as long-end yields fell 16bp.

Centene (CNC) 3Q26 results were mostly in line with a slight FY26 guidance raise. Consolidated HBR was 30bp less favorable than consensus. JPM stays Neutral on the credit, citing political uncertainty after the midterms, Medicaid rate and acuity risk.

Hilton (HLT) 3Q26 system-wide RevPAR rose 5.8% y/y, with the U.S. up 7.0% on the World Cup. Revenue was $3.325bn versus JPM's $3.377bn estimate. Softer timeshare licensing fees are a read-through for Hilton Grand Vacations. JPM stays Neutral.

INEOS Group (INEGRP) 3Q26 adjusted EBITDA was ~3% ahead of JPM's model. Capex rises about €500 million for Project One plus €200 million for existing assets, and FY26 working capital needs rise ~€180 million. Risk quoted $2-$3pts lower. JPM stays Underweight and expects the INEOS Group/Quattro spread, ~$20pt on longer-dated risk, to compress.

JetBlue (JBLU) credit: JPM was off by about $45 points on its April downgrade call on the 9.875% loyalty bonds due 2031. Management says a path remains to $1 EPS and breakeven cash flow in 2028. Fuel still determines market comfort.
Nabors (NBR) 3Q26 results were net positive, with lower FY26 capex and higher FCF guidance. Suspension of five rigs in Saudi Arabia offsets this. JPM expects bonds to trade mostly unchanged.
Nucor (NUE) 3Q26 beat expectations, and the 4Q outlook of in-line to modestly higher earnings is more constructive than consensus, which expected mid to high single digit sequential declines.
Waste Management (WM) 3Q26 was largely in line. Adjusted EBITDA was $2.12bn versus $2.16bn consensus, and gross leverage fell to ~2.9x. Revenue and FCF guidance is at the high end of range.

Whirlpool (WHR) 3Q26 missed across the board and FY26 guidance was cut on every line except OCF and FCF. JPM stays Underweight, Short Risk the 5yr CDS, and Underweight the 6.500% notes due '33 (pitched at $72.50, target $65.00).

market_movers.rationale: H&E integration risk is mostly retired and the deal should be credit accretive. Fewer high yield equipment rental bond options remain after URI reached investment grade. Prefers the 6s of '34.
Another EBITDA miss, a second FY26 guidance cut, and continued Europe pressure. Net leverage is 4.5x.
Long-term FCF visibility improves despite guidance below consensus. Expects the credit to converge toward RTX.
Custom Truck One Source (NSCO) has strong utility demand and is deleveraging. The 2L 5.5s of 2029 yield ~6.6%.
Macro and possibly terminal idiosyncratic portfolio risks outweigh a healthy forward liquidity profile.
Mostly in-line results, but Medicaid rate versus acuity risk and political uncertainty after the midterms.
INEOS Group (INEGRP) faces elevated 2027 capex that neutralizes earnings convexity, with limited line of sight to gross debt reduction.
Weak 3Q26 and broad guidance cuts. JPM sees a further FCF and net-debt shortfall and a possible downgrade into low single-B triggering index-driven forced selling. Short Risk on the 5yr CDS.

sector_views.rationale: Yields in equipment rentals and industrials are below market averages, but HRI and NSCO are preferred.
Underweight FMC and INEGRP. Likes the CE-EMN CDS trade and LYB-DOW compression.
Medicaid rate and acuity risk and political uncertainty after the midterms.

earnings_insights: Herc Rentals (HRI) 3Q26 earnings recap accompanies an upgrade to Overweight.

O-I Glass 3Q26: revenue ~$1.62bn reported (-2% y/y) versus Street estimate $1.62bn. Adjusted EBITDA reported $234m (-29% y/y) versus Street estimate $267m. Europe segment operating profit reported $2m versus $95m in 3Q25.
Boeing 3Q26 reported: results in line, FCF modestly ahead of expectations. Long-term FCF guidance for 2027-2029 is below consensus.

Johnson Controls F4Q26 reported: revenue $7.11bn versus consensus $7.03bn, adjusted EBIT $1.30bn versus consensus $1.24bn (18.3% margin versus 17.6% consensus), FCF $1.08bn versus consensus $954m. FY27 guidance: organic revenue growth 11-12% versus consensus 8.6%, and 12-14% in F1Q27 versus consensus 8.7%.
Centene 3Q26 reported: consolidated HBR 30bp less favorable than consensus, with a slight FY26 guidance raise.
Hilton 3Q26 reported: revenue $3.325bn versus JPM estimate $3.377bn, adjusted EBITDA $1,058m versus JPM estimate $1,044m. System-wide RevPAR +5.8% y/y to $124.70.
INEOS Group 3Q26 reported: adjusted EBITDA ~3% ahead of JPM's model after adjusting ~€16m of inventory holding gains. Cash generation +€268m. JPM estimates 4Q26 EBITDA at €527m and FY27 at ~€2.02bn.
Nucor 3Q26 reported: beat expectations. 4Q guided in line to modestly above 3Q.
Waste Management 3Q26 reported: revenue $6.85bn versus consensus $6.82bn, adjusted EBITDA $2.12bn versus consensus $2.16bn (31.0% margin versus 31.7% consensus), FCF $983m versus consensus $981m.
Whirlpool 3Q26 reported: missed across the board, FY26 guidance cut on every line except OCF and FCF. Holds ~$300mn FCF guide. Net debt target lowered to <$4.5bn from <$5bn.
Upcoming: FMC reports 3Q and FY27/FY28 expectations Thursday. AXTA and PPG report this week. Eastman reports Thursday and LYB reports Friday.
Nabors 3Q26 reported: net positive, with lower FY26 capex and higher FCF guidance.

risk_factors: Europe execution, pricing pressure and energy and freight costs at O-I Glass.
Managed care: unfavorable Medicaid rates or disenrollment from work requirements, and political uncertainty after the midterms.
High fuel prices and leverage for JetBlue, and Middle East uncertainty for Nabors including the Saudi rig suspensions.
Whirlpool risk of a further downgrade into low single-B and an FCF and net-debt shortfall.
INEOS elevated 2027 capex, Project One startup delay to near year end, and 2028 maturities to refinance.
FMC macro and potentially terminal idiosyncratic portfolio risks.
vol_and_positioning: LQD call implied volatility has fallen materially in October while IEF (7-10 UST) implied volatility trades sideways. LQD options are pricing negative spread-rate correlation.
CD Player notes low ETF option volatility and high EU correlation.
The hyperscaler 10s30s curve is at 86% of its 1y range. The 3s5s curve is at 71% of its 1y range.
geopolitical: Conflict in the Middle East has kept fuel prices high, pressuring JetBlue credit.
Saudi Arabia (KSA) suspended five Nabors rigs.
The AKZO-AXTA merger remedies include AXTA asset sales.

tension_points.bull_case: Upside risks are better-than-expected earnings and deleveraging from a housing recovery, further equity stake sales (WHR India, WHR China), or a potential acquisition by a competitor or private equity firm. The year-end net debt target was lowered to <$4.5bn and the ~$300mn FCF guide was held.
tension_points.bear_case: A FCF and net-debt shortfall forces a downward revision at FY results, and a further downgrade into low single-B (currently B2/B+/BB- with all Negative Outlooks) triggers index-driven forced selling.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Better-than-expected earnings and deleveraging, equity stake sales, or acquisition by a competitor or private equity firm.

tension_points.bull_case: Medicare performance positions MA to hit breakeven a year ahead of the 2027 target, and Part D membership may grow.
tension_points.bear_case: Membership disenrollment is unavoidable, and states may not raise rates enough to compensate for increased acuity, with a politically uncertain environment after the midterms.

theme_stances.evidence: We are still not covering our Underweight.
